questions.question: Air in a vertical frictionless piston-cylinder with an electrical resistor. P_atm=100 kPa; piston mass=45 kg; piston face area=0.09 m^2; air volume increases by 0.045 m^3 at constant pressure; air mass=0.27 kg; specific internal energy increases by 42 kJ/kg. The assembly is insulating and initially/finally at rest; g=9.81 m/s^2. Determine energy transferred from the resistor to the air in kJ.
questions.wording_note: The photographed question calls the requested transfer heat. For a boundary enclosing the air and internal resistor, classify the electrical energy crossing the boundary as work. State the chosen boundary consistently.

questions.question: A cooking pan with inner diameter 20 cm is covered by a 4 kg lid. Local atmospheric pressure is 101 kPa. Determine the temperature at which water starts boiling.
questions.method: Assuming the lid sustains its weight as pressure load: A=pi*D^2/4; P=P_atm+m_lid*g/A; T=T_sat(P), from Cengel A-5 with interpolation.

questions.question: A rigid vessel contains 2 kg of refrigerant-134a at 800 kPa and 120 degC. Determine vessel volume and total internal energy.
questions.method: Use Cengel A-13 at 0.80 MPa and 120 degC; V=m*v and U=m*u.

questions.question: Water initially at 10 bar and 400 degC is cooled at constant pressure to saturated vapor (1->2). The piston is then blocked and the water is cooled at constant volume to 150 degC (2->3). Sketch both processes on p-v diagrams; determine total specific work and total specific heat transfer, in kJ/kg.
questions.method: State 1: A-6 at 1 MPa and 400 degC. State 2: A-5 saturated vapor at 1 MPa. State 3: v_3=v_2; use A-4 at 150 degC to determine quality and u_3. w_out=P_1*(v_2-v_1), w_23=0, q=u_3-u_1+w_out.

questions.question: For a fixed mass of an ideal gas heated from 50 to 80 degC at constant pressure, compare required energy at 1 atm and 3 atm. Also compare heat required at constant volume and at constant pressure for the same temperature change. Explain why.
questions.transcription_note: Question number and left edge are cropped. The distinction between supplied heat and other work must follow the complete question assumptions.
questions.method: With only boundary work, constant-pressure heat is m*Delta h and is independent of pressure for an ideal gas. For the same mass and temperature change, Q_P>Q_V since c_p>c_v.

questions.question: A 0.5 m^3 rigid tank contains refrigerant-134a initially at 160 kPa and 40 percent quality. It is heated until pressure reaches 700 kPa. Determine (a) refrigerant mass and (b) heat transferred. Show the process on a P-v diagram relative to saturation lines.
questions.transcription_note: Left and bottom edges are cropped; numerical conditions and requested results are readable.
questions.method: A-12 initial mixture: v_1=v_f+0.4*(v_g-v_f), u_1=u_f+0.4*u_fg, m=V/v_1. v_2=v_1. Compare v_2 to saturation limits at 700 kPa, then obtain actual final properties from the appropriate Cengel table; Q=m*(u_2-u_1) assuming only boundary work and negligible KE/PE.

questions.question: A piston-cylinder contains 5 kg of refrigerant-134a at 800 kPa and 70 degC. It is cooled at constant pressure until it exists as liquid at 15 degC. Determine heat loss and sketch the process on a T-v diagram relative to saturation lines.
questions.source_note: An undated photographed continuation page; do not assume it follows a specific other uploaded exam.
questions.method: With only boundary work, Q=m*(h_2-h_1), Q_out=-Q. A-13 supplies h_1. A-11 at 14 and 16 degC can bracket the saturated-liquid approximation at 15 degC if the compressed-liquid approximation is justified and explicitly labeled.

questions.question: 15 kg of air in a piston-cylinder is heated from 25 to 77 degC by an internal resistance heater at constant 300 kPa. Heat loss is 60 kJ. Determine electrical energy supplied in kWh.
questions.method: W_e,in=m*(h_2-h_1)+Q_out; use Cengel A-17 ideal-gas enthalpies or an explicitly justified Cengel A-2 specific-heat approximation. Divide kJ by 3600 for kWh.

questions.question: The lower half of a 10 m high cylindrical container holds water of density 1000 kg/m^3; the upper half holds oil with SG=0.85 (density 850 kg/m^3). Determine pressure difference between top and bottom.
Complete the H2O property table and show the states on a P-v diagram.
questions.transcription_note: Only printed givens are recorded. Handwritten answers have correction marks and must not be treated as verified properties.
questions.method: Compare u with u_f/u_g at specified pressure, or T with T_sat(P); use the phase-appropriate Cengel table. Do not confuse u_fg with u.

questions.question: A rigid tank of 2.5 m^3 contains 15 kg of saturated liquid-vapor water mixture at 75 degC. The water is slowly heated. Determine the temperature when the liquid is completely vaporized and sketch on a T-v diagram with saturation lines.
questions.method: v=V/m=0.1666667 m^3/kg is constant; at complete vaporization v=v_g(T). Use Cengel A-4 with bracketing data. This is the same method and data as tutorial 2 problem 3-51.
